<thought>The proton NMR spectra show chemical shifts at 0.85 ppm (doublet of doublets, 3H), 2.04 ppm (quartet of doublets, 2H), 4.62 ppm (doublet of doublets, 1H), and 7.46 ppm (doublet of doublet of doublets, 4H). The peaks at 7.46 ppm are consistent with aromatic protons, likely from a benzene ring. The peak at 4.62 ppm suggests a proton adjacent to an electronegative atom, possibly an oxygen or nitrogen. The peaks at 0.85 ppm and 2.04 ppm suggest the presence of an ethyl group. Given this information, the compound might be an ethyl-substituted aromatic compound. To confirm the structure, I will use the IR spectra to identify any functional groups, especially those involving oxygen or nitrogen.</thought>
<action>ir_spectra</action>

<thought>The IR spectra show peaks at 3109, 3107, 3086, 3081, 3048, 3037, 3033, 2991, 2978, 2954, 1588, 1577, and 1502 cm⁻¹. The peaks around 3100-3000 cm⁻¹ are indicative of C-H stretching in aromatic rings, supporting the presence of a benzene ring. The peaks at 1588 and 1577 cm⁻¹ suggest C=C stretching in an aromatic ring. There are no strong peaks in the region typically associated with carbonyl groups (around 1700 cm⁻¹) or broad peaks for O-H or N-H stretching, suggesting the absence of these functional groups. Given the data from the NMR and IR spectra, the compound is likely an ethylbenzene derivative. I will now attempt to construct a possible SMILES string for this compound and validate it.</thought>
